title: Floating-point and integral promotion
recap: Small integral types generally promote to int before arithmetic. Promotion is a particular value-preserving conversion, not a general promise that every conversion is safe.
Keep intermediate and result storage wide enough. Assigning the promoted sum back into a small type can lose the range that promotion gave you.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement addSmall(signed char left, short right), returning their sum as int. Inputs use left in [-100,100] and right in [-30000,30000]. Do not store the result in either small input type. Integral promotion lets the arithmetic use int without losing the sum.
hints: Let the operands promote during addition.
Return the result directly as int.
A sum above the signed-char range must still be preserved.
